Alloy 454 is a precipitation-hardened nickel-base superalloy single crystal.
The gamma' phase volumetric content of Alloy 454 and Mar-M 247 was near 60%.
Alloy 454 showed greater creep rupture strength than the reference alloys, particularly at higher temperatures.
Anisotropy in tensile yield strength, creep, and creep rupture strength was most pronounced at around 760°C.
Orientations near the -111 and 011 axes showed extremely low strength compared to the 001 axis.
The tensile axis orientation was determined using Laue's reverse X-ray method.
Samples with tensile axes within 10° off-axis from the 001 axis were used for temperature dependency testing.
Orientation dependency testing was performed at 760°C and 900°C for tensile strength, and 760°C and 982°C for creep.
The gamma' phase in these alloys displayed increased strength with increasing temperature, unlike common alloys.
TEM analysis showed differences in dislocation structures and slip systems between the different orientations.
Near the -111 axis, {100}<110> and false {100}<110> slip systems developed due to the high gamma' phase strength.
Near the 001 axis, multiple slip in {111}<110> and {111}<112> systems caused work hardening from the initial creep stage.
The rupture surface of the sample near the 011 axis had an extremely smooth, 111 plane cleavage-like morphology.
The rupture surface of the sample near the 001 axis was rough and perpendicular to the tensile axis.
Alloy 454 showed a larger allowance in high strength off-axis orientation from the 001 axis compared to other alloys.
